selected.title: My Boyfriend Secretly Set Up a Loyalty Test
selected.hook: The guy hitting on me at the bar wasn't random. My boyfriend had sent him to test me.
selected.voiceover:
The guy hitting on me at the bar wasn't random. My boyfriend had sent him to test me.

We were out with friends when this stranger started chatting with me while my boyfriend was outside taking a call. I kept it polite, mentioned I had a boyfriend twice, and eventually walked back to our table.

My boyfriend looked satisfied.

The next morning, one of his friends texted me: "You passed, by the way."

I thought she meant some joke from the night before.

She didn't.

Apparently my boyfriend had asked a friend-of-a-friend to flirt with me, offer to buy me drinks, and see whether I'd give him my number. Three people in our group knew about it.

When I confronted him, he said he'd been cheated on before and just needed "peace of mind."

Then he showed me the messages planning it.

They had discussed where the guy should approach me, what he should say, and even whether he should pretend to know one of my favorite bands so I'd keep talking.

That made it worse.

I wasn't just being tested. I was being staged into a situation without knowing everyone around me was watching.

He keeps saying the result proves he can trust me now.

But all it proved to me is that he didn't trust me yesterday.

Would you forgive a loyalty test if you passed it, or is arranging one already a betrayal?

What started as insecurity turned into a planned setup involving multiple friends. Is testing a partner ever justified if trust is already shaky?
